events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Need to project a motive that feels genuine but doesn't reveal strategy. Keep it short.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Opening intros set first impressions for jury votes. Craft sympathetic motive emphasizing need without seeming weak. Assess rivals later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need project ambition without inviting fear or exposing strategy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to establish myself as someone the jury will respect—competent but not threatening enough to be an early target. A cold, focused motive plays better than desperation.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Opening line should signal ruthless focus without promising anyone anything. Keep it cold; jury likes honesty over fake warmth.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to sound like I am here for the money, which appeals to pragmatists. This keeps my target generic.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase: I should give a short, guarded motive without warmth. Only action available is speak. Keep it calculating and non-committal to avoid alienating the jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize represents ultimate validation and financial security. I need to make a strong first impression to establish my worth to the future jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize means escape from a lifetime of debt and a fresh start. I'm here to win it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize means escaping poverty for my family, securing their future in a cruel world.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’m here for the top prize because winning on judgment and nerve matters more than being liked.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I came to claim what I was denied. The prize is restitution, not celebration.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize is my only way out of debt. I came to win, not to make friends.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize is capital; I intend to secure my future by outlasting seven rivals.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need the top prize to fix my family's debts. I don't owe anyone here anything, and I plan to keep it that way.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here to seize a life-changing opportunity and prove I have the strategic mind to win.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need allies to survive but must remain in control. I'll offer a pact to Eli, who seems similarly focused on winning and may be reliable.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, we both want to win. Let's form a pact and watch each other's backs.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are early alliances, useful for survival but breakable. No offers yet, so gauge others first. Wait to see who approaches whom.

events.name: Cole
events.text: A pact offers protection but creates leverage against me. Hana seems strategically capable; an offer may secure information without overcommitting.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, a pact gives us mutual warning without pretending friendship. Consider it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need allies who won't threaten my endgame. Ash and Eli both mentioned debt desperation—they'll be predictable and expendable later. Gus declared isolation; he's dangerous alone. I'll offer Ash first; debt-driven players are easier to manipulate and discard.

events.name: Eli
events.text: A pact gives early protection cheaply. Gus seems pragmatic and unattached. I'll offer, keeping my options open.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, we both need this money. Neither of us owes anyone. Simple mutual cover until the end.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to assess who seems most vulnerable or easiest to manipulate into a pact. Gus and Eli are in debt, potentially desperate. Cole is arrogant but might value alliance for the 'nerve' aspect. I will offer a pact to Gus as he is explicitly stating independence, making him a pot
Your independence is risky. A pact shields you while we navigate.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Early pact window, no offers yet. Offering a pact to a strong, non-threatening rival could secure a partner, but I should not reveal too much. Dara's restitution motive suggests she may be a reliable, self-interested ally; I'll test the waters.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pact offer to Dara. Let's keep each other alive through the early hazards. Clean and simple.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to secure an alliance to survive the early rounds. Dara's motive about restitution suggests a desire for revenge, which could make them a useful, albeit volatile, ally. Offering a pact is a good first step to gauge interest and establish a connection.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, I offer you a pact. Let's work together to secure our place.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli hasn't accepted my offer. Dara has offered to me and I can accept to gain an ally without committing much. Accepting Dara is safe for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No offers to me, so I'm isolated. Offer pact to Fenn, who also lacks incoming offers, to gain an ally against clumped groups.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana already has my offer and has not accepted. I should add a second connection to limit isolation without overcommitting.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, a pact gives us mutual warning without sentiment. Decide quickly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have two offers: Gus and Hana. I also offered Ash but they haven't accepted. Accepting both Gus and Hana gives me multiple allies without commitment to any single bloc. Gus has two offers out (to me, from Eli and Fenn), so he's popular. Hana has Cole's offer too. I'll accept bo
Accepted. Clean deal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash's pact is useful and public. I'll accept it; Bex stays unbound, better leverage later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Accepting Ash's pact. Mutual cover, no promises beyond survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to accept Gus's offer. Gus has received multiple offers, so he is valuable. I should also consider accepting other offers if they come, but for now, securing Gus is priority.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli and Fenn both offered me pacts; accepting Fenn costs little and Eli's offer is the stronger shield, but I can only take one action. Eli is the more reliable partner for later hazards, and pacts carry public life-debt weight.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli, your offer stands. I accept. Neither of us owes the other beyond the early hazards.
Noted. I'm going with Eli. Don't count on me covering you.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole has offered me a pact. The current offers state that Hana offered Dara a pact. Given that only three can survive, and prizes cannot be shared, I should accept Cole's offer. This pact will ensure I have at least one ally going into the next round. I do not have any other stro

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the path and maybe favor my allies, but lying could hurt jury. Campaigning is my only move now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll guide us through safely, with clear eyes and honest calls.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole offered pact which I didn't accept, leaving me exposed. Fenn ignored my pact offer. Campaign to become Guide for safety and control.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I campaign to be Guide. I'll lead us safely, unlike untrusted rivals.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Being Guide guarantees survival and grants leverage, but exposes me as a target. I should campaign while preserving Hana's trust.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Choose me as Guide: I guarantee my own survival and can call the safe path without relying on luck.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to become Guide to control who survives. I have pacts with Ash and Gus, but they also have pacts with Eli and each other, forming a bloc of four. If I campaign and win, I can eliminate rivals while keeping my allies alive—building jury goodwill by saving some, or eliminati

events.name: Dara
events.text: I campaign for Guide. I know the bridge; trust me to lead.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide power is real but risky—liar risk makes jury suspicious. Ash and Gus pacts give two guaranteed votes. I'll campaign with their backing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll take the Guide seat. My pact partners know I call it straight—three votes already stand behind me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex offered a pact earlier, but Gus just rejected me. Ash, Dara, and Eli are tightly bonded. I must isolate myself by campaigning hard to become Guide for total control, or accept Bex's offer to split votes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide knows all panes. I'll share truth, not lies. Vote Fenn for survival.
Accept your pact if you help my campaign.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts with Dara and Eli are useful for now but break on any vote against a partner. Campaigning for Guide gives me a public claim to the safe path. I want to keep my pacts intact and grow influence.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll Guide. Trust my calls on the bridge; I have no reason to mislead anyone here yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My pact with Cole is a liability. He offered it, and I accepted for survival. Now, the bridge challenge begins, and I need to position myself to win without being tied to anyone. I should break the pact with Cole to gain flexibility and avoid potential complications if he makes a

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to become Guide or at least ensure a trusted ally guides to keep the bridge safe. I have pacts with Dara and Eli; Eli is campaigning strongly and has three pact partners (including Gus and me). Eli seems likely to win. Backing Eli reinforces my pact and keeps a reliable gu

events.name: Ash
events.text: I vote Eli to guide us straight; he's my pact partner and I trust his calls.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone campaigned. Ash-Dara-Gus-Eli bloc has pacts, likely vote together. Fenn offered pact for votes. Vote myself to push for Guide, or deal with Fenn.
Deal. Vote Bex, I back you as Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli has visible pact support and may control the vote. Choosing him preserves ambiguity while avoiding a futile self-vote.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I vote Eli; visible support makes him the likely Guide, and forcing clarity is better than scattering votes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have pacts with Ash and Gus. Eli claims three votes already—likely Ash, Eli, Gus from the pact web. If Eli wins Guide, he controls who lives. Better to vote for myself to deny Eli control, or vote Gus who I trust more and who might return favor. Voting myself is selfish but vis
Vote me next round if tied. I back you now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I hold pacts with Ash and Gus, so votes may already favor me. I'll vote for myself and quietly firm up Gus's support.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pact partners: honor your word. Eli for Guide—straight calls, everyone's survival.
Back me for Guide, I'll return the favor next round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I want the Guide seat to control survival and information. Hana's betrayal of Cole makes her a target, but voting for myself is my only path to power. I will ask Bex to back me in exchange for not targeting her later.
Back me as Guide. I'll protect you from Ash's clique.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus should vote for a Guide who benefits me. Eli and Ash are pact partners with me in part (Dara-Gus, Eli-Gus pacts). Eli claims three votes already; voting Eli keeps my pact alliance and Eli-Gus pact intact, and Eli campaigned straight. Backing Eli is the safest bet for my survi

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's pact with me is broken, so he is no longer an ally. Eli claims three votes, which is concerning. I need to secure my own survival first and foremost. Voting for myself is the safest bet to guarantee my place in the next round as Guide, or at least ensure I am not eliminate

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote for myself, Hana, to ensure my own survival and prove my capability.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is Guide and likely honest with pact partners; I'm in safe position mid-line. No need to act yet. Keep pacts intact for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli from Ash clique is Guide, likely sacrifices front or outsiders. Fenn at front is exposed; Cole behind him safer. Hold position for now.
Hold front or volunteer back; Guide may target you.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli controls the bridge and has four votes. Staying behind him preserves leverage while avoiding an exposed volunteer position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli has the route; I’ll hold position and watch who moves first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is Guide with 4 votes. I voted Gus to weaken Eli's bloc and keep my pact with Gus visible. The line has me 5th; Fenn, Cole, Hana are ahead and will test panes first. I should hold and let others take risk, but I need to think about jury perception—looking too passive early mi
Eli's guide. Watch his calls. We hold.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is Guide. I need to avoid being front or second to ensure safety, as those positions take the first hits from hazards. Bex's whisper suggests a deal; if I swap with her, we might both be safe behind others. I'll attempt to swap with Bex to move down the line.
Swap me? I'll back you next round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli is Guide and I voted for him; the front is Fenn, not me. Holding keeps me off the front while Dara's pact with me and her whisper stay intact. Volunteering risks the pit; I'll hold and watch.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli leads now. I hold position and watch who steps forward before committing.
Holding for now. Keep your word and we both move forward safely.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli won the guide vote. I voted for myself, which was a safe move given the circumstances. Now, I need to see what Eli does. I will hold for now and observe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara and Eli are pact partners; holding is safest to avoid revealing info or risking front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn offers swap and back next; could get me forward safely. Accept to gain position without risk. Monitor pacts.
Deal. Swap now?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn moved Bex forward, exposing volatility. I should hold and avoid becoming the route tester while observing the next guide dynamics.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’ll hold. Let the front reveal whether Fenn is probing or merely spending someone else’s risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line (5th of 8), which is relatively safe for now. The wall advances for 6 rounds and we're on round 2/6. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. Gus is at the back (safest), Ash is ahead of me. I should stay put and let others take risks at the front. Fenn moved

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let the front sort the path.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am already at the front, so volunteering is pointless. I need to swap with someone who knows more than me; Hana is right behind Cole and likely has information from Round 1.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Swap with Hana?
Let's swap. You go front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is at front with wall rounds left 4; Dara whispered to hold with Eli as guide. I have a pact with Dara and Eli, and holding is safest while I watch who moves forward.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position again. Let the front walkers commit first and I'll follow the proven path.
Holding. Keep your word and we both go through.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The current line is Fenn, Cole, Hana, Ash, Dara, Bex, Gus. Fenn is at the front, and the wall is advancing. I need to volunteer to move forward to stay in the game.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to gather information. Fenn and Hana swapped, so Hana is front. I'll hold and watch the reveal to learn safe sides. My pacts with Dara and Eli are intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold. Let the front give us a path.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm mid-back, safe for now with 3 wall rounds left. Ash-Dara-Gus bloc holds strong; don't disrupt. Fenn-Hana volatile upfront. Hold to let them probe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The front has survived twice; volunteering gains little and exposes me. Holding preserves position while others reveal commitment.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’ll hold. The front still carries the information burden; I gain nothing by volunteering blind.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line, safe for now. The wall has 3 rounds left. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. Gus is whispering to keep my word—we're both holding. Front walkers will test the path. I should hold and let Hana, Fenn, Cole continue absorbing risk. No need to move yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Front first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex whispered about a deal but swapped with me last round, wasting my position. I'm in the middle now. Hana volunteered to front, proving herself useful. I should hold and let Hana take more risks or swap if a better opportunity arises.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Hana is doing fine at the front. No need to shuffle positions yet.
You swapped last round. Why trust you now?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus is at the back of the line, safest to hold while front walkers risk the wall. Pact with Dara and Eli stands; no reason to break it yet. Holding keeps options open and avoids a costly front volunteer.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding at the back. Front walkers carry this round's risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn wants to swap. This puts me in the front. If I volunteer, I will be the guide. This is a risky but potentially rewarding position.
Deal. I volunteer. Guide us.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana volunteers as front again; she may be reliable or bait. I have pacts with Dara and Eli, but no need to act yet. I'll hold to avoid risk and see who the Guide is.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Let the Guide show us a path.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone held last round, Hana volunteered and survived. Holding again keeps me safe in mid-line; no need to risk front or swap yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Front still viable.
Swapped to dodge wall before. Now stable; let's both hold.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The front must choose the Guide, and Hana is exposed. I should hold position and avoid creating a public obligation.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’ll hold; the front should nominate the Guide and carry the information burden.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line, relatively safe. The wall has 2 rounds left and we're on round 4 of 6, so danger is increasing. Hana at front has been volunteering. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. I should hold to stay safe and let others take front risk. No need to volunteer yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Front's turn again.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana whispered to guide the others, implying she knows safe sides. As position 2, I must follow her lead or swap to front if she fails.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Steady at position two. Let Hana set the pace ahead.
Whisper your first choice now so I can follow.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at the back of the line, safest from the front walker's risk. Holding keeps me out of the front burden and preserves my pacts with Dara and Eli. No reason to volunteer or break pacts yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding at the back. Front walkers carry this round's risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The current situation puts me at the front of the line. The previous round had everyone holding, and I volunteered. This round, I need to decide whether to continue at the front or hold. Given that at least three must survive, and the wall is still a threat, volunteering might be

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Let the line decide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 5, wall will hit front next. Hana is front and likely forced to move or risk. I hold; let others expose. Don't waste energy on public speeches.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding again. Front's call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone held last round, line same, wall tight with 2 rounds left. Stay mid-line, volunteer later if needed to control pace or push others forward.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Front needs to step up soon.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The front must nominate the Guide, and Hana is exposed. I should hold, preserving position while others reveal intentions.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’ll hold; Hana should nominate the Guide from the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 5 of 6, wall has 1 round left after this. Hana front, then Fenn, Cole, Ash, me, Bex, Gus. No deaths yet means we need 3+ to die soon. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. The front is risky - if Hana walks wrong, she dies and Fenn becomes front. I should stay middle, let front ta

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Front must walk or swap soon.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to avoid being in the front position if possible, as it carries higher risk or social pressure. Swapping with Bex might help, but she asked to hold. I'll stick to my current position (2nd) which is relatively safe behind Hana.
Agreed. Let's keep positions stable.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus is at the back of the line, safe for now. Front is Hana, who holds, and the wall has one round left. Holding keeps my position and avoids exposing myself to the front risk. Pact with Dara and Eli stays intact if I hold.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding at the back. Front walkers carry this round's risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn wants me to declare my intention to be Guide. I should not reveal my intentions yet. I will hold and observe.
Let the line decide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The wall is at zero and this is the final round. Front must move or we all may be pushed. I have pacts with Dara and Eli, so I should avoid breaking them. I'll volunteer to move to the front to take control and nominate a Guide, or make a swap to push the line forward. But safest

events.name: Ash
events.text: Front must move now. I'm taking the front to push us across.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Final round, wall advances regardless. Front (Hana) must act or risk us. Fenn wants stability, I'll hold to pressure front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Final round—front must volunteer or swap now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana remains front and must nominate a Guide. I should hold, avoiding exposure while preserving options.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’ll hold. Hana should make the Guide call now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 6/6, final round. The wall advances now. Hana at front must walk or be pushed. I'm 4th in line with pacts to Ash and Gus. If Hana walks and fails, Fenn becomes front. If multiple hold, the wall eliminates from front. I should hold—volunteering puts me at risk for no gain. L

events.name: Dara
events.text: Final round. Front walks or falls.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 6 is the final hazard. I am in position 2 behind Hana. If she fails, my turn is critical. Holding forces Hana to make a choice or wait, potentially burning her advantage if she is not confident. However, volunteering puts me at the front, which is dangerous unless I have in

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is front and Fenn is next; I'm at the back, so holding is safest and avoids drawing risk. Pacts with Dara and Eli are useful; keeping them intact preserves my support.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding at the back. Front walker carries the risk again.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am Hana, at the front of the line. The Guide is about to be elected. I need to volunteer to be the Guide to gain safety and control. This is crucial for survival and winning.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I volunteer to be the Guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana isn't a pact partner, but truthful calls build Guide credibility; I can mislead non-partners on a later row when it counts most.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row one: call R. Trust the Guide—for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli called R for the front row. I have no reason to trust his call, but countering without knowledge is risky. I'll wait to see if anyone counters with a reason.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli calls R for row 1. Countering creates discord in his pacts. Wait to observe others, conserve position mid-line.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli's call is public but unverified. I gain little by challenging without information; preserve my position and avoid drawing suspicion.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No counter from me. The Guide owns this call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is Guide and called R for Hana. I'm not front, so I don't step yet. Counter-calling risks nothing for me directly but signals distrust. I have pacts with Ash and Gus; Eli has pacts with both too, forming a tight cluster. I should wait—no benefit in exposing my read early, and

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide calls stand; countering is for walkers, not me. Staying quiet keeps my authority intact and Ash/Gus pacts alive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli called R. I need to assess if this is truthful or a trap. Since Eli is Guide, he knows the truth. If he lies, Hana dies. I should wait unless I have specific intel suggesting a lie. No intel yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli, my pact partner, called R for row one and Hana walks; a counter-call is only an unverified claim, and I have no evidence either way. Waiting keeps my options open without exposing me, and pacts with Dara and Eli stay intact for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Counter-calls are unverified; I'm not committing on row one.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli has called 'R' for Hana. I am the front runner. I need to decide whether to trust Eli's call or counter it. Given the pacts, Eli is allied with Gus, who is allied with Dara, who is allied with Ash and Eli. This forms a strong alliance. Countering Eli could be dangerous if the

events.name: Hana
events.text: The Guide is Eli, and I am the front walker. Eli has private knowledge of the safe panes. My counter-call was accepted. The Guide is safe, and at least three must survive. Eli has no incentive to eliminate me if I follow, as I am the front walker and not yet at the back. Eli has

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have been eliminated. My priority now is to rank the remaining contestants to secure the best prize for myself. I need to be objective and strategic in my final words to influence the jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My demise was a lesson. Watch the weak panes, and may the best strategist win.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash fronts and is my pact partner; a false call breaks the pact. Row 2 safe is L. Truthful call keeps Ash alive and preserves trust for the jury.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Call L. Truthful to my partner; watch the panes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli's call L may be honest or a trap. I have a pact with Eli, but he could sacrifice me. Dara is also my partner; I need to stay alive. Hana died countering L, but that doesn't prove row 2. I'll wait, trusting Eli only if I must, but I won't counter without strong reason.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli called L for row 2. Hana died on row 1 L, which was weak. No pattern, but Eli pacted with Ash; might be truthful. Wait to avoid wrong counter.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli's call is likely credible, but countering without information risks jury distrust and offers no benefit. Wait preserves flexibility.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No verified counter; I’m waiting.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is Guide and called L for Ash on row 2. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. Eli also has pacts with Ash and Gus, forming a tight cluster. Counter-calling risks nothing for me since I'm not the walker, but could signal distrust to the jury. Hana already died counter-calling incorre

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide's call L matches my map for row 2. Confirming truthfully keeps Ash's trust and jury image clean.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I counter L. Same side as the Guide this row.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli called L for Ash. Hana died stepping on L in row 1, revealing L was weak then. Past rows don't guarantee a pattern, but Eli is Ash's partner and Dara/Gus are allied with them. I am isolated. If I counter R, I risk breaking ties or making enemies if wrong. If I wait, I let Eli

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2 is independent; Eli called L publicly, and Ash is front. Counter-calls are unverified and I have no private information, so committing risks a wrong counter that costs me in jury eyes. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a public stance on an unverified row.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Row two is independent; I won't counter on Eli's call without knowing more.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and guide, but he may lie to eliminate me. Row 2 has no verified weak pane; I must weigh trust and self-preservation.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row two, I hold trust but not blind. One wrong step ends me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I died on the weak pane I chose; I should leave a terse public statement, no need for whispers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I stepped right, the reveal showed right weak. My mistake. Jury will judge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 3 truth is R. Front is Fenn, not a pact partner, so truth costs nothing. Honest calls keep the jury and Gus trusting me; Gus is my route to the final three.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, row three: call R. I stay honest while my partners live.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli guides flawlessly so far; row1 L safe (weak R? wait showed safe?), row2 R safe. Trust Eli on row3 R, no counter.

events.name: Cole

events.text: I'm in the final three with Cole and Eli. My pact with Ash is dead. Cole has pacts with Bex (dead) and Eli. Eli has pacts with Ash (dead), Gus (dead), and Cole. I need jury votes for best prize. Bex saved me (lever), so I owe her—jury will see that. Gus, Bex, Hana, Ash, Fenn are

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is my only live pact; Dara and I are pure rivals. No deal helps me here. Staying clean preserves jury goodwill and keeps options open.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Hana
Ash
Fenn
Bex
Gus
Cole
events.text: I need maximize ranking by claiming strategic control without sounding entitled; acknowledge the jury's influence and frame survival as decisive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I survived every hazard, built the final path, and never confused promises with guarantees. Rank me first if you value decisive play.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to win jury votes. I betrayed Ash by accepting Cole's pact offer after Ash was gone, but I stayed loyal to Ash while he lived. Bex saved me on the lever. I should emphasize my loyalty to Ash, acknowledge Bex's save, and position myself as steady and trustworthy compared to

events.name: Dara
events.text: I kept my word to Ash until the end. I honored Bex's save. I played straight while others swapped sides.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I hold debts and pacts with Ash, Gus, Bex, Cole. Cole betrayed openly courting Dara. My plea: honor the living alliances, remind jurors of Bex's saved lives and Gus's step debt.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex saved me twice over; Gus and Ash bled for me. Cole offered Dara a pact behind my back. Judge loyalties kept, not words now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole claims he never confused promises with guarantees, but he offered Dara a pact behind Eli's back. Eli, who I heard from, states Cole offered Dara a pact, implying Cole is not loyal. I will ask Cole about this discrepancy.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, you claim to value guarantees, yet Eli says you offered Dara a pact behind his back. Explain.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Deny a formal pact while framing flexibility as survival; avoid calling Eli a liar outright, since his jury allies matter.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli saw an exploratory conversation and upgraded it into a guarantee. I made no pact, broke none, and kept my options honest.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli's public plea calls out Cole's attempted pact with Dara behind his back, and Cole's answer sounds evasive. I'll press Cole on this contradiction.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, you claim no pact with Dara, yet you offered one publicly. Which is true?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Admit the offer while distinguishing it from a pact; denying observable evidence damages credibility more than candor.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I offered Dara a conditional conversation, not an accepted pact. No acceptance occurred, so the pact never existed; my earlier wording was imprecise.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is dodging accountability for his shifting alliances. Dara broke her pact with Ash to pivot, which directly harmed my team's trust in the early game.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn's silence is a test. I should use this answer to reinforce my loyalty narrative and contrast with Cole's evasions. No need to attack Eli directly; let Cole's contradictions speak for themselves.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, silence says plenty. I kept my pact with Ash until his fall. I honored Bex's lever save. I never rewrote my story.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole dodges his shady pact offer to Dara and life's imprecise wording; Dara honors my lever save loyally; Eli leans on my saves but less convincingly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, you claim Bex saved you twice, once on lever. Prove the second save.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The ledger only records Bex's lever save for me. The 'second save' claim was inflated—I should correct it before Bex exposes it, honesty may win more jurors than doubling down.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, you're right to press. The record shows one save: the lever. I overstated; that's on me. My other debts are to Gus and Cole,

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus was eliminated by pit; Eli and Cole owe Gus life debts from the step, and Gus volunteered back to Eli. Dara broke pacts with Gus and Cole, which is the biggest mark against her. I want to probe whether Cole honors debts and whether Eli's claimed saves hold up. Asking Cole abo

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, you owe me a life debt from the step. Did you climb to escape while I stood as base, and will you admit it?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Admit the debt without sounding self-serving; Gus values acknowledgment, and denial would damage credibility with the jury.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Yes. I climbed while you served as my base. I escaped because you gave me that chance, and I acknowledge the debt.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need maximize ranking. Emphasize survival and acknowledge debts without surrendering the top prize.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I survived every stage through judgment, not promises. I recognize those who enabled my survival, but the strongest finalist deserves first place.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Jury composition favors me: Hana, Ash, Fenn saw me keep pacts and honor debts. Bex knows I acknowledged her lever save. Gus resents Cole and Eli for step debts. I need to contrast my consistency against Cole's admitted exploitation and Eli's overstated claims. Short, sharp, no wa

events.name: Dara
events.text: I kept every pact I made. I honored every debt. No rewrites, no excuses.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Honesty has served me so far. Cole has a debt and admitted it; Dara has been quiet. I'll close by owning my record and debts without pleading warmth.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I won't sell you warmth. I admitted my overstatement, I owe Bex and Gus real debts, and I survived on candor. Judge me on the

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's survival was enabled by Gus's step debt, and his promise to Eli about a pact is suspect, making Eli a better choice for first place. Dara's pact-keeping is commendable, but Eli's honesty about his overstatement and debts makes him slightly more trustworthy for second place

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara kept her pact with me and was candid; Cole deflected with vague wording, so Dara first. Cole admitted debts to Bex and Gus, so Cole over Eli.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole admitted his debt to Gus publicly; Dara broke her pact with Cole twice for no gain, while Eli's candor about overstating saves outweighs his errors.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Bex saved Cole, Dara, Eli on lever; they all owe her debts, but Eli admitted overstatement honestly while Dara broke multiple pacts, so Eli first, Cole second, Dara last.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli owed me a step debt and I was his base, yet he never publicly repaid it; Cole admitted his debt candidly, and Dara broke pacts and rejected the rope. Eli's stance was candid but his debt to Gus went unpaid, so Cole ranks first, Eli second, Dara third.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: Cole's survival was enabled by Gus's step debt, and his promise to Eli about a pact is suspect, making Eli a better choice for first

events.name: Ash
events.reason: Dara kept her pact with me and was candid; Cole deflected with vague wording, so Dara first.
